history: Traditionally said to date to the reign of Emperor Korei. The shrine gave its name to the district of Omiya ('great shrine') and was designated the ichinomiya of Musashi Province. Its 2km approach (sando) is among the longest in Japan.
why_visit: The central Hikawa shrine of the Kanto region and the source of the Hikawa network's worship of Susanoo. The long tree-lined approach and the vermilion Romon gate make it a serene retreat within greater Tokyo.
prayer_focus: Matchmaking and good marriage (縁結び), warding off misfortune, and family safety.
best_season: Early summer for fresh greenery along the approach; the August Reitaisai festival.

history: Founded in the 7th century as Gion-sha, the shrine became the cult center of the Gion faith that arose to placate epidemics. It was renamed Yasaka Shrine in 1868 during the Meiji separation of Buddhism and Shinto (shinbutsu bunri).
why_visit: The head shrine of roughly 2,300 Yasaka/Gion shrines nationwide and the spiritual home of the Gion Matsuri, one of Japan's three great festivals. Its vermilion West Gate above Shijo-dori is a defining Kyoto landmark.
prayer_focus: Protection from epidemics and misfortune (厄除け yakuyoke), prosperity in business (商売繁盛), and good fortune.
best_season: July for the Gion Matsuri; cherry blossoms in adjacent Maruyama Park in early April; lantern-lit evenings year-round.
